title: Integrate CI baseline runner for token throughput regressions
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Background: We currently run ad-hoc perf benchmarks in CI but lack a robust baseline comparison and automated PR gating for throughput (tokens/sec) and latency p95 regressions. This ticket scopes adding a CI baseline runner that (1) executes a controlled set of microbenchmarks on a stable hardware pool, (2) stores time-series of key metrics, (3) computes statistically-informed regressions versus an evolving baseline, and (4) blocks PR merges when regressions are reproducible. Goal: reduce unnoticed performance regressions and give engineers fast feedback on throughput/latency impact of code changes.
acceptance_criteria: A dedicated CI job 'perf/ci-baseline' runs on GPU runners with pinned docker image and seeds
Baseline window is maintained in GCS and updated nightly; comparisons use last N good runs (default N=10)

Regression detection evaluates tokens/sec and p95 using 95% confidence (bootstrap + robust median-of-means), and marks 'regression' when drop/increase exceeds thresholds and is statistically significant
PR gating: If regression detected, CI fails the perf job and posts a formatted GitHub Status + comment with links to diffs and raw artifacts
Artifacts (raw traces, aggregated stats, flamegraphs, CPU/GPU utilization) are uploaded and linked in the CI job log
False positive rate controlled: at most 1 blocking flake allowed in last 5 runs before triage, and flaky runs are recorded but do not immediately block merges
tasks: Design benchmark harness and canonical workloads (prefix distributions, typical seq lengths)
Implement CI job that runs stable docker image on dedicated GPU pool with warmup iterations
Add storage layer for baselines in GCS with metadata: commit, model, runner image
Implement statistical comparison library (bootstrap + MOM) and alpha configurable per-metric
Integrate gating logic with GitHub checks + Slack alerting channel #perf-regressions
Create Grafana dashboard and nightly job to refresh baselines and surface flaky tests
baseline_strategy: Use rolling baseline of latest N good runs (N configurable; default 10). Each baseline run is the median across K repeated trials to reduce noise. Nightly baseline refresh job promotes stable runs into the baseline if they pass data quality checks (no OOMs, stable GPU utilization). Baseline metadata includes runner image, model hash, and sequence-length distribution.
test_schedule: PR-level quick harness (smoke perf) + post-merge full run. Quick harness runs a small canonical batch (3 seeds x 2 repeats) to catch large regressions. Full run executed on merge or nightly uses larger sample sizes for statistical confidence.
gating_rules: Fail PR if tokens_per_sec decreases by >=5% with p < 0.05 AND p95 latency increases by >=10% with p < 0.05. For borderline cases (5-8% tokens/sec drop) attach an informational check and require a dev acknowledgement. Allow one flaky blocking failure in last 5 runs before requiring manual triage.
rollback_plan: If a perf regression blocks production rollout, the release engineer can pin the runtime to the previous known-good model/image and open a rollback PR. Automated fallback in runtime routing will redirect traffic to the last baseline-qualified variant until revalidation.
notes: Decisions from spike: we prefer bootstrap CIs + median-of-means over raw t-test because perf distributions are heavy-tailed. Use fixed seeds and synthetic prompt prefixes representative of production (collected from anonymized telemetry). We have a prototype PR for statistical library at github.com/redwood-inference/bench-utils/pull/17. See design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/CI+Perf+Baseline+Design
